ESTJ>INTJ.title: Someone who plans this week with next year in mind.
ESTJ>INTJ.body: You get today's work done quickly and plan ahead with the future in mind. When you make your monthly schedule, you work backward from a deadline six months out and decide what to do this week. Some days you lead discussions in front of everyone, and some days you want to think alone. Before a meeting, you might go somewhere quiet to sort out your thoughts.
ESTJ>INTJ.body_s: You get today's tasks done quickly and plan ahead with the future in mind. Even your study schedule for tests is worked out backward from the day of your entrance exams, and you decide which pages to cover this week. Some days you lead discussions in front of everyone, and some days you want to think quietly alone. Before a meeting for a group presentation, you might go somewhere quiet by yourself to sort out your thoughts.
ESTJ>INTJ.do: On the train to work, you sort out next month's plans on your phone.
ESTJ>INTJ.do_s: On the train to school, you sort out next month's plans on your phone.
ESTJ>INTJ.worry: On days you lead in front of people, you want more alone time than you expected. It takes you a while to decide whether to stick with the way you've always done it or try a new way.
ESTJ>INTJ.karai: When someone says "Anywhere's fine," you pick a place in five minutes and even make the reservation.
ESTJ>INTJ.aru: You get this week's tasks done quickly, while in the back of your mind you're thinking, "Where will this be in three years?"
ESTJ>INTJ.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energy from being with people and thinks things through based on past experience. As the years went by, you also came to recharge with time alone and to imagine what's ahead. Your hands are as quick at getting things done as ever, while your head now looks a little further down the road. With tasks you're used to, your hands keep going on their own, and your free mind naturally starts thinking about a few years from now.

ESTJ>INTP.title: Someone who quickly asks, "Why is that?"
ESTJ>INTP.body: You don't just take what you're told as it is. You wonder, "Why?" Even when something is decided in a meeting, it doesn't feel settled to you until you understand the reason. At work you follow the set steps properly, but you're always wondering whether there's a better way. Even when watching the news, you look things up yourself, thinking, "Is that true?"

ESTJ>INTP.do: You compare phone plans from different companies and switch to a cheaper one.
ESTJ>INTP.do_s: When you shop online, you compare prices at several stores and buy from the cheapest one.
ESTJ>INTP.worry: You want to follow the set way, but you also want to try your own way, and it leaves you uneasy. When you've been talking with people day after day, you want time to think alone.

ESTJ>INTP.aru: You do your work by the manual, but inside you keep thinking, "Wouldn't it be faster to do these steps the other way around?"

Through all kinds of experiences, you started spending more time lost in thought alone, and even with things already decided, you began to wonder, "Is there another way?" Your ability to follow steps is still very much there. You're so used to working through steps by hand that your mind is free in the meantime, and it starts searching for a faster way.

ESTJ>ENTJ.body: You check how things have been done before, then think of something new. Even when you pitch a new plan, you talk with a sheet summing up last year's numbers and lessons right in front of you. At work, the one who looks back at last year's way and says, "Let's change this part this year," is usually you.

You know a trip won't go wrong as long as you cover the classic sights, so with the time left over, you feel like trying one small adventure.

ESTJ>ENTP.title: Someone who throws out ideas and decides who's in charge on the spot.
ESTJ>ENTP.body: You keep throwing out ideas and move the conversation forward on the spot. While listening to someone in a meeting, you think of another option: "Then we could also do it this way." Sometimes you want to change what was decided, but in the end you see it through. Even on a trip with friends, you're the one who finally says, "Okay, let's go with this."

Once a reservation is made and the plan is settled, your mind starts looking for the next option, and on the day itself, a different restaurant starts to look better.

ESTJ>INFJ.title: Someone who keeps things on track and checks on anyone who seems down.
ESTJ>INFJ.body: You keep work moving smoothly, but you also pay close attention to how the people around you are doing. You tell everyone about deadlines early, and when you have a hard favor to ask, you wait until the other person has a free moment. After a meeting, you might ask someone who didn't say much, "What did you think back there?"

ESTJ>INFP.do: You started a hobby just because you liked it, and now you've set monthly goals and you're taking it seriously.

ESTJ>ESTJ.karai: Even on days off, as soon as you wake up you decide the order of what to do today.
ESTJ>ESTJ.aru: On a trip with friends, you put the schedule together and send it to the group chat without being asked, and the night before you send the meeting time once more.
ESTJ>ESTJ.why: Your temperament and character are the same combination, so your natural love of planning shows up just as it is in how you go about each day. Whatever you're doing, you first want to make the schedule and roles clear. Getting energy from working with people has been true since way back. If plans stay vague, it seems like someone will run late or get lost, and heading that off ahead of time is what makes you feel most at ease.
ESTJ>ESTJ.yure: Your temperament and character match, so your result doesn't change much. Still, if you take it on a day you want to relax alone or you're tired, your answers may come out a little different.
ESTJ>ESTJ.plus: You get irritated because you want everyone to see it through together. When you're around, things finish on schedule.
ESTJ>ESTJ.tip: When asking someone for something, first ask them, "By when do you think you can do it?" A deadline they set themselves is easier for them to keep.
ESTJ>ESTJ.hidden: Do you feel relieved on days you spend quietly alone? Getting your energy back with time alone is something you can do, too. Make some alone time now and then, and you'll feel more at ease around people.

ESTJ>ESFJ.title: Someone who runs things tightly and looks out for each person.
ESTJ>ESFJ.body: When everyone does something together, you run things tightly and keep them on schedule. But you also think carefully about how each person feels. When picking a restaurant, you first think back to who enjoyed which dish at the last get-together. Even when setting up a tent at a barbecue, you think about where it goes so no one ends up sitting in the sun.
ESTJ>ESFJ.body_s: When everyone does something together, you run things tightly and keep them on schedule. But you also think carefully about how each person feels. When your class decides something, you first think back to who had a hard time at the last event. Even when setting up the tents for sports day, you think about where they go so no one ends up sitting in the sun.
ESTJ>ESFJ.say: "The farewell party is $30 each. I've already ordered the flowers."
ESTJ>ESFJ.say_s: "The send-off party for the seniors is $5 each. I've already ordered the flowers."
ESTJ>ESFJ.do: After fairly assigning work duties, you quietly take over for someone who looks unwell.
ESTJ>ESFJ.do_s: After fairly assigning cleanup duties, you quietly take over for someone who looks unwell.
ESTJ>ESFJ.worry: You often end up organizing or in charge, and your days to rest keep shrinking. After picking a place or an order, you keep wondering, "Was that really right?"
ESTJ>ESFJ.karai: You're strict about rules, but you're the softest on anyone in trouble.
ESTJ>ESFJ.aru: You almost picked the restaurant because "it's close to the station," but in the end you chose again because "my friend would probably like this one."
ESTJ>ESFJ.why: By birth, you're the type who uses logic to choose the most efficient option. As the years went by, you came to care just as much about whether the people with you are happy. Logic is still what comes to mind first. A reason like "it's close to the station" comes to you right away, but what settles it in the end is "Will my friend enjoy it?", so you end up choosing the restaurant all over again.
ESTJ>ESFJ.yure: Only one part is different: deciding with logic or with feelings. Answer thinking about setting rules at work and you lean toward logic. Answer thinking about looking after friends or family and you lean toward feelings.
ESTJ>ESFJ.yure_s: Only one part is different: deciding with logic or with feelings. Answer thinking about setting rules on a student committee and you lean toward logic. Answer thinking about looking after friends or family and you lean toward feelings.
ESTJ>ESFJ.plus: You go back and forth because you care about both rules and people. With an organizer who's firm and kind, everyone feels at ease joining in.
ESTJ>ESFJ.tip: Before taking on someone else's work, ask yourself once, "Could I ask someone else to do this?" Things will still run without you carrying it all.
ESTJ>ESFJ.hidden: When choosing a place or splitting the bill, can you quickly decide, "This one's cheaper and closer"? That's your temperament, which decides with logic. When feelings make you hesitate, comparing this way makes it easier to decide.

ESTJ>ISTP.title: Someone who gives instructions, then goes to fix it themselves.
ESTJ>ISTP.body: You're good at asking people to "do it this way," but before you know it you're doing it with your own hands. Rather than read the manual, you just start working on it while remembering what you did before. Some days you want things to go as planned, and some days you want to handle it on the spot. When the copier at work jams, you might be the first one to go take a look.
ESTJ>ISTP.body_s: You're good at asking people to "do it this way," but before you know it you're doing it with your own hands. Rather than read the manual, you just start working on it while remembering what you did before. Some days you want things to go as planned, and some days you want to handle it on the spot. When the classroom projector stops showing anything, you might be the first one to go take a look.
ESTJ>ISTP.say: "Well, if it breaks, we'll figure it out then."
ESTJ>ISTP.do: When assembling furniture, you read the manual, then switch to your own way halfway and finish faster.
ESTJ>ISTP.worry: When you've been leading people for days, you want to quietly work with your hands on your own. Even jobs you've handed off bother you, and you end up going to fix them yourself.
ESTJ>ISTP.karai: The one thing you don't want your family to move is where your tools go.
ESTJ>ISTP.aru: After a meeting where you lead everyone, you suddenly go quiet and want to rush home and play games or cook alone.
ESTJ>ISTP.aru_s: After a club meeting where you lead everyone, you suddenly go quiet and want to rush home and play games or cook alone.
ESTJ>ISTP.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energy from being with people and brings everyone together to move forward as decided. Through all kinds of experiences, you also came to recharge with time alone working with your hands. You can still handle being the one who brings everyone together, but that's time that uses up your energy. While you're leading, you keep talking and looking out for people, so when it's over, the words stop coming and you want to recharge by working with your hands alone.
ESTJ>ISTP.yure: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your leading-at-work self or your making-something-alone-on-a-day-off self.
ESTJ>ISTP.yure_s: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your leading-your-club self or your making-something-alone-on-a-day-off self.
ESTJ>ISTP.plus: You go fix things yourself because you notice trouble right away. With someone who can give instructions and use their hands, the work doesn't stop.
ESTJ>ISTP.plus_s: You go fix things yourself because you notice trouble right away. With someone who can give instructions and use their hands, the group's work doesn't stop.
ESTJ>ISTP.tip: On days you're in charge, choose one person who can keep watch while you go fix something. That way, the whole thing keeps going.
ESTJ>ISTP.hidden: When you start something, do you naturally set up the steps? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Use it, and you can carry the fixes you came up with on the spot over to next time.

ESTJ>ISFP.title: Someone who's very organized, but takes their time choosing cute little things.
ESTJ>ISFP.body: On your days off, you take your time watering and caring for the plants you love. You notice even a slight change in the color of a leaf and move the plant to a better spot. At work, you set the steps and get things done quickly.
ESTJ>ISFP.body_s: On your days off, you take your time watering and caring for the plants you love. You notice even a slight change in the color of a leaf and move the plant to a better spot. With school assignments, you set the steps and get things done quickly.
ESTJ>ISFP.say: "Oh, this cup is such a nice color."
ESTJ>ISFP.do: You tidy your room fast, but you just can't decide where to put your decorations.
ESTJ>ISFP.worry: Switching between quick, busy time and slow time wears you out. Even with things you love, you think "I have to do this right," and some of the fun goes away.
ESTJ>ISFP.karai: You pick a place by its star rating, then score it yourself while you eat.
ESTJ>ISFP.aru: Café hopping is supposed to be just for fun, but you catch yourself counting: "That's the fifth one this month."
ESTJ>ISFP.why: Valuing what's right in front of you and how things feel to the touch is the same in your temperament and your character. The three that differ are how you deal with people, how you decide, and how you go about things. By birth, you're the type who gets energy from being with people, decides with logic, and sticks to a plan. Through all kinds of experiences, you also came to value time alone doing what you love and going with your mood. Even when you think you're just having fun, your natural habit of feeling settled when you count and keep records shows up, and you end up counting how many cafés you've been to.
ESTJ>ISFP.yure: Three things differ between your temperament and your character, so your result can change a lot. You may get different types depending on whether you picture yourself at work on a weekday or doing your hobby on a day off.
ESTJ>ISFP.yure_s: Three things differ between your temperament and your character, so your result can change a lot. You may get different types depending on whether you picture yourself at school on a weekday or doing your hobby on a day off.
ESTJ>ISFP.plus: You think "do it right" because you're serious about what you love too. You keep at it, so you keep getting better at it.
ESTJ>ISFP.tip: A few times a month, have a hobby day where you don't count how many or how long. On that day, you don't need to worry about whether you did it right.
ESTJ>ISFP.hidden: By nature, you think things through with logic before deciding. When a shop you like has something new, don't you think about the price and how often you'd use it before buying? If you ever want to turn something you love into work, that same thinking helps you find a way to keep it going.

ESTJ>ESTP.title: Someone who makes solid plans, then changes them on the day.
ESTJ>ESTP.body: You make solid plans, but on the day you adjust to what's happening. You check the map and the weather before you head out, so once you arrive you can pick your next stop without hesitating. Even if something happens, you can quickly figure out your next move. Even if it starts raining at a barbecue, you're quick to say, "Okay, let's move under the roof."
ESTJ>ESTP.say: "This is the plan. But if it rains, we'll change it on the spot."
ESTJ>ESTP.do: When a friend invites you to golf, you're at the driving range by the next weekend.
ESTJ>ESTP.do_s: When a friend invites you to play pickup soccer, you've bought cleats and started practicing by the next weekend.
ESTJ>ESTP.worry: You want to keep to your plans, but you also want to change them on the spot, and you worry you're jerking people around. You're not good at sitting still, so even on days off you want to do something.
ESTJ>ESTP.karai: By the morning of the day, you've already changed the plans you made.
ESTJ>ESTP.aru: You researched your trip carefully, but once you get there you say, "This looks more fun," and change several plans.
ESTJ>ESTP.why: By birth, you're the type who makes plans and sticks to them. As you gained experience, you also came to enjoy heading toward whatever looks fun in the moment. Your habit of looking things up in advance is still there, just as it was. Because you've done your research, you can quickly compare how fun a place you find on the spot looks, so you can change plans without hesitating.
ESTJ>ESTP.yure: Only one part is different: sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture a work deadline and you answer like a planner. Picture heading out for fun and you answer like someone who goes with the flow.
ESTJ>ESTP.yure_s: Only one part is different: sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture a homework deadline and you answer like a planner. Picture heading out for fun and you answer like someone who goes with the flow.
ESTJ>ESTP.plus: You want to change things on the spot because you quickly notice a better way. With someone who can plan and move fast, everyone feels safe when something comes up.
ESTJ>ESTP.tip: When you change plans, tell everyone, "I'm just changing this part." Then they can follow along with peace of mind.
ESTJ>ESTP.hidden: Do you get up at the same time every morning and get ready in the same order? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Because of it, even when you change plans on the spot, you don't drop the important things.

ESTJ>ESFP.title: Someone who prepares carefully, then has the most fun on the day.
ESTJ>ESFP.body: You run the preparations for a get-together carefully, then have the most fun on the day. You figure out how much to buy based on how many people came last time and how much was left over. Even on a trip, you're the one who says between stops, "Let's stop by here."
ESTJ>ESFP.say: "When we're done cleaning up, let's all have ice cream."
ESTJ>ESFP.do: During big cleanups, you put on music and get everyone going while you tidy up quickly.
ESTJ>ESFP.worry: You want everyone to have fun so much that you sometimes don't notice you're tired. Some days you go back and forth between wanting to do things properly and wanting to go with the mood.
ESTJ>ESFP.karai: While you're deciding the karaoke order, you run out of time to sing yourself.
ESTJ>ESFP.aru: At a birthday party, you run everything from setup to the program, but when the cake comes out, you're singing the loudest.
ESTJ>ESFP.why: By birth, you're the type who uses logic to set the plan and sticks to it. As you gained experience, you also became able to go right along with the fun mood of the moment. You switch clearly between preparing and enjoying. Because you've finished preparing properly and your part is done, by the time the cake comes out you can relax and sing the loudest.
ESTJ>ESFP.yure: Two parts are different: deciding with logic or with feelings, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Answer as your preparing-at-work self and the result comes out structured. Answer as your hanging-out-with-friends self and it comes out softer.
ESTJ>ESFP.yure_s: Two parts are different: deciding with logic or with feelings, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Answer as your preparing-for-a-school-event self and the result comes out structured. Answer as your hanging-out-with-friends self and it comes out softer.
ESTJ>ESFP.plus: You forget you're tired because you're happy seeing everyone enjoy themselves. When you run things, the get-together stays on time, so everyone can relax and have fun.
ESTJ>ESFP.tip: When you're asked to prepare for a get-together, hand just one task to someone else. You'll still have time to enjoy yourself.
ESTJ>ESFP.hidden: When choosing a place, do you quickly compare, "Which is cheaper?" That's your temperament, which decides with logic. Use it, and fun plans can move forward without strain.

ESFJ>INTJ.title: Someone who finds the fastest way and helps until others get the hang of it.
ESFJ>INTJ.body: You always think of the fastest way to get things done and stick to the plan. But you also keep an eye on whether the people around you are having trouble. On your lunch break, you might walk alone while thinking about the next steps. When a new way of doing things is decided at work, you stay by the side of people who aren't used to it yet and teach them.
ESFJ>INTJ.body_s: You always think of the fastest way to get things done and stick to the plan. But you also keep an eye on whether the people around you are having trouble. During breaks, you might think alone about how the next practice should go. When your club decides on a new way to practice, you stay by the side of younger members who aren't used to it yet and teach them.
ESFJ>INTJ.say: "This way is fastest. I'll help until you get the hang of it."
ESFJ>INTJ.do: You plan the family trip alone and fit in one place each person wants to visit.
ESFJ>INTJ.worry: Some days you want to think alone, and some days you want to look after everyone, and you can't decide which. After deciding firmly, you worry you came across as cold.
ESFJ>INTJ.karai: You tell others, "Take your time," but you get there 10 minutes early yourself.
ESFJ>INTJ.aru: You turned down a friend's invite and spent the day thinking alone. It was relaxing, but at night you feel a little guilty.
ESFJ>INTJ.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energy from being with people and decides by going along with how others feel. As the years went by, you also came to recharge with time alone to think and to decide with logic. These days you have both the wish for time alone and the wish to value the people who invite you. Even when you're satisfied after a relaxing day alone, at night the face of the person you turned down comes to mind, and you feel like you did something a little wrong.
ESFJ>INTJ.yure: Three of the four parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answering as your planning-alone self or your looking-after-everyone self can give totally different results.
ESFJ>INTJ.plus: You worry you seemed cold because you care about people. Someone who teaches the fast way and helps until others get used to it is someone people rely on.
ESFJ>INTJ.tip: On days you turn down invites to be alone, decide first: "Today's a rest day." You can relax without feeling guilty.
ESFJ>INTJ.hidden: When you go to a gathering, do you get more energy than you expected? That's your temperament, which gets energy from people. Plans you made alone get even better when you talk them over with others.

ESFJ>INTP.title: Someone who thinks things through, then answers with others in mind.
ESFJ>INTP.body: You think things through and come up with an answer that makes sense. But you also worry about whether that answer will cause trouble for anyone. With online reviews, you read and compare several to find the answer that makes the most sense. When someone in your family can't figure out how to use an appliance, you come up with an easy explanation and teach them.
ESFJ>INTP.say: "That makes sense. But would anyone have trouble with it?"
ESFJ>INTP.do: When you hear people's schedules don't match, you quietly find a day everyone can make and send it.
ESFJ>INTP.worry: After being honest, you worry you hurt the other person. Sometimes you go back and forth between wanting to think alone and wanting to go along with everyone.
ESFJ>INTP.karai: You're the one who keeps worrying the longest about the thing you said you "don't really mind."
ESFJ>INTP.aru: When you all go on a trip, you look up the cheapest, fastest way to get there and check with each person that it's OK.
ESFJ>INTP.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energy from being with people, goes along with how everyone feels, and moves forward as decided. Through all kinds of experiences, you also came to look things up alone and use logic to find the best answer. All four letters are different, so you have both the fun of looking things up and the wish to look out for everyone. Even if you find the cheapest, fastest way to get there, whether it really makes everyone happy is a separate question, so you want to check with each person.
ESFJ>INTP.yure: All four parts are different, so your result can change a lot each time. Answering as your thinking-alone self or your chatting-with-friends self could give opposite results.
ESFJ>INTP.plus: You worry because you care about people. Someone who shares well-thought-out answers with the other person in mind is someone people trust.
ESFJ>INTP.tip: When you share an honest opinion, end by asking, "What do you think?" Knowing how they feel means you won't worry so much at night.
ESFJ>INTP.hidden: Do your thoughts come together while talking with people? That's your temperament, which gets energy from people. Try talking through what you thought about alone, and your answers will get even better.

ESFJ>ENTJ.title: Someone who sets clear goals and moves forward with everyone.
ESFJ>ENTJ.body: You set clear goals and lead everyone forward. At the start of the year you set goals, and each month you check together, "Look how far we've come." Some days you say tough things, but you also keep a close eye on how everyone is doing. When someone on the team has a birthday, you might quietly have a cake ready.
ESFJ>ENTJ.say: "Let's continue the goal talk over lunch together."
ESFJ>ENTJ.do: When planning a big project, you've already booked the restaurant for the wrap-up party.
ESFJ>ENTJ.do_s: When planning your class's school festival booth, you've already booked the restaurant for the after-party.
ESFJ>ENTJ.worry: You want to decide clearly, but when someone seems unhappy, you can't. You go back and forth between putting the goal first and putting everyone's feelings first.
ESFJ>ENTJ.karai: You're strict about goals, but you take forever choosing snacks to bring for everyone.
ESFJ>ENTJ.aru: On the day a big project wraps up, you care less about whether it went to plan and more about whether everyone's worn out.
ESFJ>ENTJ.aru_s: On the day the school festival wraps up, you care less about whether it went to plan and more about whether everyone's worn out.
ESFJ>ENTJ.why: By birth, you're the type who values past experience and the feelings of the people around you. As you gained experience, you also came to set goals and lead people with logic. Becoming a stronger leader didn't make your care for people any weaker. While you're working toward a goal, you're looking ahead, but the moment it's over, your attention turns to how the people who worked hard with you are doing.
ESFJ>ENTJ.yure: Two parts are different: facts or ideas, and deciding with logic or with feelings. Picture work goals and you lean toward ideas and logic. Picture time with your team and you lean toward facts and feelings.
ESFJ>ENTJ.yure_s: Two parts are different: facts or ideas, and deciding with logic or with feelings. Picture your team's goals and you lean toward ideas and logic. Picture time with your teammates and you lean toward facts and feelings.
ESFJ>ENTJ.plus: You can't decide because you care about everyone's feelings. People want to follow someone with clear goals who also watches out for them.
ESFJ>ENTJ.tip: When it's hard to decide, make the decision smaller: "Let's decide this much today and the rest next week." The talk keeps moving.
ESFJ>ENTJ.hidden: Do you notice small changes in your teammates and ask, "How've you been?" That's your temperament, which decides with feelings. Use it, and even with tough goals, everyone can work without pushing too hard.

ESFJ>ENTP.title: Someone who gets the conversation going and comes up with slightly unusual ideas.
ESFJ>ENTP.body: You love talking with people, and while you talk you come up with unexpected ideas. You soften the mood so everyone finds it easy to speak up. When opinions split, you line up each side's reasons and think about which makes the most sense. When a meeting stalls, you might change the flow by saying, "Can I bring up something a little different?"
ESFJ>ENTP.body_s: You love talking with people, and while you talk you come up with unexpected ideas. You soften the mood so everyone finds it easy to speak up. When opinions split, you line up each side's reasons and think about which makes the most sense. When a class discussion stalls, you might change the flow by saying, "Can I bring up something a little different?"
ESFJ>ENTP.say: "What if we look at that problem from the other way around?"
ESFJ>ENTP.do: When helping at the neighborhood festival, you chat with everyone who comes while working the front desk.
ESFJ>ENTP.worry: When the conversation gets lively, you end up saying too much and regret it later. You go back and forth between keeping the usual way and trying a new one.
ESFJ>ENTP.karai: Even for a dish where you were told "plain is fine," you can't help adding a little twist.
ESFJ>ENTP.aru: You were listening to a friend's problem, but halfway through, suggesting "What if you tried this?" gets fun, and you end up doing all the talking.
ESFJ>ENTP.why: By birth, you're the type who stays close to how the other person feels and listens carefully. Through all kinds of experiences, you also discovered the fun of getting new ideas from conversations and building them up with logic. Even when you mean to be the one listening, when an idea comes to you, you want to share it. When you see something like "this might work" taking shape in someone's problem, the wish to hand it to them comes first, and you end up talking too long yourself.
ESFJ>ENTP.yure: Three of the four parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answering as your debating-with-friends self or your looking-after-family self can give totally different results.
ESFJ>ENTP.plus: You can reflect on saying too much because you think about the other person's feelings. When someone makes it easy to talk and also brings new ideas, discussions become fun.
ESFJ>ENTP.tip: When the talk heats up, pause and ask, "By the way, what do you think?" You'll know how they feel before you say too much.
ESFJ>ENTP.hidden: Do you remember what your friends like and what they told you before? That's your temperament, which trusts facts and experience. Use it, and you can shape new ideas to fit the person.

ESFJ>INFJ.title: Someone who really cheers on a friend's job change or move.
ESFJ>INFJ.title_s: Someone who really cheers on a friend's future plans or move.
ESFJ>INFJ.body: When a friend is struggling, you think together with them about what to do next. The week after they come to you, you send a message: "How's it going since then?" You like lively get-togethers, but afterward you also want some quiet time alone. When you hear a friend is moving, you might look up good restaurants in their new town for them.
ESFJ>INFJ.say: "I'm sure there's a workplace that suits you better."
ESFJ>INFJ.say_s: "I'm sure there's a path that suits you better."
ESFJ>INFJ.do: When a friend asks for advice about changing jobs, you look for good openings and send them.
ESFJ>INFJ.do_s: When a friend asks for advice about what to do after graduation, you look up campus visit days at schools that might fit and send them.
ESFJ>INFJ.worry: You think about other people's worries as if they were your own, and it wears you out. After a lively time, you're confused by how suddenly you want to be alone.
ESFJ>INFJ.karai: Even before the trip destination is decided, you're already looking up places everyone would love.
ESFJ>INFJ.aru: You love lively dinners with friends and enjoy them to the end, but the moment you get home, you suddenly want to be alone.
ESFJ>INFJ.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energized by being around people. As the years went by, you started thinking about what people feel deep down, and your time to recharge shifted toward being alone. You still love lively get-togethers. You want to quietly sort through, at home, all the conversations and feelings you took in during the dinner, so the moment you get home, you want to be alone.
ESFJ>INFJ.yure: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and facts or ideas. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your having-dinner-with-friends self or your thinking-alone-at-home self.
ESFJ>INFJ.plus: It wears you out because you truly think about the other person. Having a friend who thinks things through with you that much is reassuring.
ESFJ>INFJ.tip: On days you've listened to someone's worries, put your phone down when you get home and take a long bath. You'll reset and be ready to listen again the next day.
ESFJ>INFJ.hidden: Do you feel your energy rising as you talk with friends? That's your temperament, which gets energy from people. Use it, and instead of worrying alone, you can find answers by talking with others.

ESFJ>INFP.title: Someone who loves looking after people and values time alone too.
ESFJ>INFP.body: You love looking after the people around you. When a friend seems tired, you might buy a drink they'd like on the way home and hand it to them. But you also really value time alone doing what you love. On the evening of a day off, you might be slowly sipping tea while watching a favorite movie.
ESFJ>INFP.say: "You can keep eating, but there's something I'd like to talk to you about."
ESFJ>INFP.do: After taking care of family errands, you spend the night relaxing alone with your favorite music.
ESFJ>INFP.worry: You can ask what others want to do, but you find it hard to bring up what you want. When you've been going along with everyone for a while, you want to be alone.
ESFJ>INFP.karai: You tell others, "Do whatever you like," but you can't say it to yourself.
ESFJ>INFP.aru: After lunch with friends, you stop by a bookstore alone on the way home and take your time picking a book.
ESFJ>INFP.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energy from being with people and sticks to the plan. Through all kinds of experiences, you also came to recharge with time alone, lost in the things you love. These days, you can't do without either time with people or time alone. During lunch you're enjoying yourself while looking out for the other person, so the time alone at a bookstore on the way home makes a perfect little break.
ESFJ>INFP.yure: Three of the four parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answering as your looking-after-family-and-friends self or your doing-what-you-love-alone self can give totally different results.
ESFJ>INFP.plus: You can't bring it up because you think about everyone's feelings first. When someone like you says, "I want to do this," the people around you will surely cheer you on.
ESFJ>INFP.tip: Once a week, tell someone you trust one thing you want to do. Saying it out loud helps you start doing it, little by little.
ESFJ>INFP.hidden: Do you settle the date and place for get-togethers early? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Use it, and you can put what you want to do on your schedule and make it happen.

ESFJ>ENFJ.title: Someone who takes on the yearly events and makes them better.
ESFJ>ENFJ.body: You take on events that bring everyone together and make them a little better every year. Before the planning meeting, you reach out first to the people who helped last year. Even at the neighborhood summer festival, you use last year's lessons and add one more activity for kids.
ESFJ>ENFJ.body_s: You take on events that bring everyone together and make them a little better every year. Before the planning discussion, you ask the older students who helped last year what was hard. Even at the school festival, you use last year's lessons and add one more activity for the kids who come.
ESFJ>ENFJ.say: "If it's okay with everyone, I'll be on the committee this year."
ESFJ>ENFJ.say_s: "If it's okay with everyone, I'll be on the planning committee this year."
ESFJ>ENFJ.do: When a younger coworker is handed their first task, you keep an eye on them until it's done and ask, "How's it going?" a few times.
ESFJ>ENFJ.do_s: When a younger club member is handed their first job, you keep an eye on them until it's done and ask, "How's it going?" a few times.
ESFJ>ENFJ.worry: While doing things for everyone, some days you don't notice you're overdoing it. Sometimes you can't decide whether to keep the usual way or add something new.
ESFJ>ENFJ.karai: You ask, "Can anyone do this?" and when everyone goes quiet, you raise your own hand.
ESFJ>ENFJ.aru: You run the yearly event exactly like last year. On the way home after it's over, you're already saying, "Next year, let's try this too."
ESFJ>ENFJ.why: By birth, you're the type who's good at keeping to last year's way of doing things. As you gained experience, you also started picturing what's ahead: "Next time, if we do it this way, people will be even happier." While running this year's event, you're also seeing what next year's could look like. On the way home after an event, everyone's happy faces are still fresh in your mind, so a way to make people even happier next time naturally comes to you.
ESFJ>ENFJ.yure: Only one part is different: whether you go by facts and experience or by ideas. Picture preparing for a yearly event and you lean toward facts. Picture what you want to do from now on and you lean toward ideas.
ESFJ>ENFJ.plus: You overdo it because you want everyone to be happy. With someone who takes on events and makes them better every year, everyone can look forward to next year too.
ESFJ>ENFJ.tip: When you take on a role, ask someone for help with just one thing at the start: "Could you take care of this part?" You won't have to push yourself alone.
ESFJ>ENFJ.hidden: Do you remember how things went before, like "Last year it was like this"? That's your temperament, which trusts facts and experience. Because of it, even when you add something new, the event still runs smoothly.

ESFJ>ENFP.title: Someone who books the usual place, then invites you to a new one next.
ESFJ>ENFP.body: You love being with people, and when you find something fun, you invite people right away. When you invite someone, you first think about a time and place that's easy for them. You like your usual places, but when a new restaurant opens by the station, you check the menu as you walk by. When you meet friends on a day off, the topics keep changing, and before you know it, it's evening.
ESFJ>ENFP.say: "I love your haircut! Where'd you get it done?"
ESFJ>ENFP.do: For family birthdays, you come up with a different surprise every year.
ESFJ>ENFP.worry: There are so many fun things that you pack your schedule too full and get tired. Some days you can't decide between the usual way and something new.
ESFJ>ENFP.karai: You're careful with reservations and payments, but picking an outfit takes you the longest.
ESFJ>ENFP.aru: You book the usual place for lunch with friends, but on the way home you're already saying, "Next time, that new café."
ESFJ>ENFP.why: By birth, you're the type who values familiar places and plans you've made. Through all kinds of experiences, you started noticing new things and came to enjoy deciding on the spot too. You love both the familiar places where you feel at ease and places you don't know yet. It's precisely because you're satisfied after a long talk at your usual place that next time you want to enjoy the same kind of time somewhere new.
ESFJ>ENFP.yure: Two parts are different: facts or ideas, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture preparing for yearly events and you answer in a structured way. Picture hanging out with friends and you answer more freely.
ESFJ>ENFP.plus: You overpack your schedule because you love spending time with people. Because you invite everyone, there are more fun plans for all.
ESFJ>ENFP.tip: When making plans, set one "nothing" day each week first. You won't get worn out, and you can look forward to the next fun thing.
ESFJ>ENFP.hidden: Do you always take care of reservations and payments properly? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Because of it, even when you invite people on a whim, everyone can come with peace of mind.

ESFJ>ISTJ.title: Someone who's accurate at work and quick to check on people in trouble.
ESFJ>ISTJ.title_s: Someone who turns in everything right and is quick to check on people in trouble.
ESFJ>ISTJ.body: You do your work by the rules and without mistakes. Before turning in paperwork, you check once more the spots where you made mistakes last time. But when someone nearby is having trouble, you notice right away and talk to them. You like talking with people, but quiet time to work alone matters to you too. On a rainy day, you might lend a coworker without an umbrella the spare one you keep at work.
ESFJ>ISTJ.body_s: You do your assignments and turn things in by the rules and without mistakes. Before turning something in, you check once more the spots your teacher corrected last time. But when someone nearby is having trouble, you notice right away and talk to them. You like talking with people, but quiet time to work alone matters to you too. On a rainy day, you might lend a friend without an umbrella the spare one you keep at school.
ESFJ>ISTJ.say: "The paperwork is fine. More importantly, you look pale. Are you sleeping?"
ESFJ>ISTJ.say_s: "I already turned in the handout. More importantly, you look pale. Are you sleeping?"
ESFJ>ISTJ.do: After doing your expense report by the rules, you quietly leave a throat lozenge on a coworker's desk.
ESFJ>ISTJ.do_s: After tallying the club dues by the rules, you quietly leave a throat lozenge on a friend's desk.
ESFJ>ISTJ.worry: Some days you're torn between following the rules and helping people, and you can't decide. When you've been talking with people day after day, you want some quiet time alone.
ESFJ>ISTJ.karai: You keep booking the places everyone liked last time, so the staff know your face by now.
ESFJ>ISTJ.karai_s: You keep booking the same place for class parties because everyone liked it, so the staff know your face by now.
ESFJ>ISTJ.aru: After turning in your own paperwork by the book, you help a struggling new hire go over theirs too.
ESFJ>ISTJ.aru_s: After turning in your own assignment by the book, you help a struggling friend go over theirs too.
ESFJ>ISTJ.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energy from being with people and acts based on how others feel. As the years went by, you also came to work alone by the rules and judge things with logic. Finishing your own part properly is a way of working you picked up later. When you finish your own work first, you have room to spare, so when you see someone in trouble, your natural love of helping kicks right in.
ESFJ>ISTJ.why_s: By birth, you're the type who gets energy from being with people and acts based on how others feel. Through school life, you also came to do your assignments alone by the rules and judge things with logic. Finishing your own part properly is a way of working you picked up later. When you finish your own assignments first, you have room to spare, so when you see a friend in trouble, you can't leave them alone and want to lend a hand.
ESFJ>ISTJ.yure: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and deciding with logic or with feelings. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your working-alone self or your chatting-with-coworkers self.
ESFJ>ISTJ.yure_s: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and deciding with logic or with feelings. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your working-alone self or your chatting-with-classmates self.
ESFJ>ISTJ.plus: You're torn because you care about both rules and people. Someone who works accurately and checks on people in trouble is trusted at work.
ESFJ>ISTJ.plus_s: You're torn because you care about both rules and people. Someone who does their assignments accurately and checks on people in trouble is trusted in class.
ESFJ>ISTJ.tip: Decide the order ahead of time: "First do it by the rules, then look for ways to help." You won't keep thinking about it after you get home.
ESFJ>ISTJ.hidden: Does chatting with coworkers brighten your mood? That's your temperament, which gets energy from people. Use it, and it'll be easier to talk to someone about work you've been carrying alone.
ESFJ>ISTJ.hidden_s: Does chatting with classmates brighten your mood? That's your temperament, which gets energy from people. Use it, and it'll be easier to talk to someone about assignments you've been carrying alone.

ESFJ>ISFJ.title: Someone who moves first so everyone can have a good time.
ESFJ>ISFJ.body: You move first and get things ready so everyone can have a good time. You even remember a friend once saying, "I'm cutting back on sweets," when you choose what snacks to serve. You do step in front of people sometimes, but you also like quiet time to prepare alone. On days you have people over, you might have the right number of slippers ready the day before.
ESFJ>ISFJ.say: "If anyone's cold, I've got lap blankets ready."
ESFJ>ISFJ.do: When you hear a friend is in the hospital, you go visit right away with a magazine and drink they'd like.
ESFJ>ISFJ.worry: While going along with everyone, your own plans and feelings get put last. After a day of working hard in front of people, you don't get your energy back until you relax alone.
ESFJ>ISFJ.karai: While going around asking, "Aren't you cold?" you forget to put on your own jacket.
ESFJ>ISFJ.aru: You cheerfully emcee the welcome party, but you've actually asked the new hires ahead of time what they can't eat and quietly had the dishes changed.
ESFJ>ISFJ.aru_s: You cheerfully emcee your club's welcome party for new members, but you've actually asked the newcomers ahead of time what they can't eat and quietly changed the food order.
ESFJ>ISFJ.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energized by being around people. As you gained experience, you also came to feel settled with quiet time preparing alone. These days, acting cheerful in front of people and preparing behind the scenes both come naturally to you. You know that whether newcomers enjoy themselves depends a lot on the food, so before you emcee, you want to check even what foods they don't like.
ESFJ>ISFJ.yure: Only one part is different: getting energy from people or recharging alone. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your emcee-or-organizer self or your preparing-alone-at-home self.
ESFJ>ISFJ.plus: You put yourself last because you think about everyone's feelings first. Thanks to your preparing, get-togethers always go smoothly.
ESFJ>ISFJ.tip: Before matching everyone's schedules, tell them the days you can't make first. Your own plans will be protected too.
ESFJ>ISFJ.hidden: Does your mood brighten as you talk with people? That's your temperament, which gets energy from people. Use it, and you can share what you prepared behind the scenes in a fun way with everyone.

ESFJ>ESTJ.title: Someone who wraps up discussions and checks in with each person after.
ESFJ>ESTJ.body: You wrap up discussions efficiently and make decisions on time. Before a discussion, you write down what wasn't decided last time and work through it in order. Once things are decided, you also keep each person's feelings in mind. After roles for a get-together are set, you might tell someone who didn't get what they wanted, "You'll get first pick next time."
ESFJ>ESTJ.body_s: You wrap up discussions efficiently and make decisions on time. Before a discussion, you write down what wasn't decided last time and work through it in order. Once things are decided, you also keep each person's feelings in mind. After club roles are set, you might tell someone who didn't get what they wanted, "You'll get first pick next time."
ESFJ>ESTJ.say: "We'll go with this plan. Does anyone have anything left to say?"
ESFJ>ESTJ.do: You fairly split the family chores, then take over for whoever's tired: "Just for today."
ESFJ>ESTJ.do_s: You fairly split the work for a group project, then take over for whoever's tired: "Just for today."
ESFJ>ESTJ.worry: After being direct, you worry you said it too harshly. You go back and forth between wanting people to follow the rules and wanting to be kind to them.
ESFJ>ESTJ.karai: After strictly pointing something out, you quietly leave the person's favorite snack on their desk.
ESFJ>ESTJ.aru: You said what was right, but when the other person goes quiet, you spend the whole night wondering, "Did I say it the wrong way?"
ESFJ>ESTJ.why: By birth, you're the type who thinks first about how the other person feels and chooses your words. As you gained experience, you also came to say what's right clearly, with logic. When you speak, logic comes first, and your feelings catch up after you've said it. When you see the other person go quiet, you feel you may have hurt them more by how you said it than by what you said, and it stays on your mind until that night.
ESFJ>ESTJ.yure: Only one part is different: deciding with logic or with feelings. Answer thinking about making decisions in a meeting and you lean toward logic. Think of family or friends and you lean toward feelings.
ESFJ>ESTJ.yure_s: Only one part is different: deciding with logic or with feelings. Answer thinking about making decisions in a class discussion and you lean toward logic. Think of family or friends and you lean toward feelings.
ESFJ>ESTJ.plus: You think about it all night because you don't want to damage the relationship. When someone who can say what's right also cares how they say it, it's easier to hear.
ESFJ>ESTJ.tip: When pointing something out, start by saying, "I just have one request." The other person can get ready to listen and is less likely to go quiet.
ESFJ>ESTJ.hidden: When someone's down, do you notice right away and go to them? That's your temperament, which decides with feelings. Use it, and even when saying hard things, you can say them in a way that gets through.

ESFJ>ESFJ.title: Someone who looks out for the people around them wherever they are.
ESFJ>ESFJ.body: Wherever you are, you keep checking whether the people around you are having a good time. At get-togethers, you remember who likes what, and before ordering drinks you might ask, "The usual?" At work, you might ask someone new, "Want to go to lunch together?"
ESFJ>ESFJ.body_s: Wherever you are, you keep checking whether the people around you are having a good time. When you go out together, you remember who likes what, and at the snack stand you might ask, "The usual?" In class, you might ask a student who just transferred in, "Want to eat lunch together?"
ESFJ>ESFJ.say: "There's more, so tell me if you need seconds."
ESFJ>ESFJ.do: You keep your friends' birthdays in your calendar and send a message every year.
ESFJ>ESFJ.worry: You worry about people's reactions, and some days small things bring you down. Some days you put everyone first so much that you lose track of what you want to do.
ESFJ>ESFJ.karai: You remember everyone's favorite drinks, but forget to order your own.
ESFJ>ESFJ.aru: When one person's reply in the group chat is short, you wonder, "Did I upset them?" and it bugs you all day.
ESFJ>ESFJ.why: Your temperament and character are the same combination, so the way you look out for how people are doing has shown up just as it is since way back. When everyone seems to be having fun, you get energized too. On the other hand, if even one person seems down, you can't take your eyes off them. You even remember how long everyone's replies usually are, so when just one person's is short, you notice right away and it keeps bothering you until you know why.
ESFJ>ESFJ.yure: Your temperament and character match, so your result doesn't change much. Still, if you take it on a day you're tired of people and want to be alone, your answers may come out a little different.
ESFJ>ESFJ.plus: You worry about people's reactions because you're sensitive to their feelings. When you're around, people feel cared for.
ESFJ>ESFJ.tip: If someone's reply is short, don't worry about it right away. Sleep on it. The next day, you'll usually find it was nothing.
ESFJ>ESFJ.hidden: Do you feel calm on days you spend relaxing alone? Getting your energy back with time alone is something you can do, too. Make some alone time now and then, and you won't worry so much about people's reactions.

ESFJ>ISTP.title: Someone who helps with their hands before finding words.
ESFJ>ISTP.body: When someone's in trouble, you help with your hands before you find the words. You remember where every tool and battery in the house is, and you have them out before anyone asks. You like get-togethers, but quiet time to work alone matters to you too. If a shelf in a friend's room is wobbly, you might tighten the screws without saying a word.
ESFJ>ISTP.say: "Let me see that. I think it can be fixed right here."
ESFJ>ISTP.do: At family gatherings, you end up fixing the glitchy TV or Wi-Fi alone.
ESFJ>ISTP.worry: You're not good at putting feelings into words, so when you want to comfort someone, you sometimes can't find what to say. Some days you want to stick to the plan, and some days you want to act on the spot, and even you get confused.
ESFJ>ISTP.karai: When someone thanks you, you get shy and say quickly, "Oh, it was just luck."
ESFJ>ISTP.aru: When a friend is down, you can't find the right words, so for now you buy their favorite snack and hand it to them.
ESFJ>ISTP.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energy from being with people and acts with the other person's feelings in mind. Through all kinds of experiences, you got better at working with your hands than talking, and quiet time alone became important to you too. Wanting to cheer people up has been part of you all along; the way you show it has shifted from words to actions. You know handing over someone's favorite snack gets your feelings across better than searching for the right words, so you go buy one first.
ESFJ>ISTP.yure: Three of the four parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answering as your fixing-something-alone self or your looking-after-everyone-at-a-gathering self can give totally different results.
ESFJ>ISTP.plus: You can't find the words because your body moves before your mouth. The kindness of quietly fixing things or handing over a favorite snack really does come across.
ESFJ>ISTP.tip: After fixing something for someone, add just, "Let me know if anything else comes up." Even with few words, your feelings get through.
ESFJ>ISTP.hidden: Do you notice right away when someone's feeling low? That's your temperament, which decides with feelings. Use it, and you can not only help with your hands but also just be there for them.

ESFJ>ISFP.title: Someone who looks after everyone, then takes a break alone.
ESFJ>ISFP.body: You love looking after the people around you. On days friends come over, you buy a single seasonal flower and set it on the table. After spending time with people, you take a break alone by listening to favorite music or having a cup of tea. When you go shopping, you might end up buying one cute plate you hadn't planned on.
ESFJ>ISFP.say: "I love this dish. The color is so gentle."
ESFJ>ISFP.do: When having friends over, you plan the menu ahead, but pick the table flowers on the day by mood.
ESFJ>ISFP.do_s: When having friends over, you plan the snacks ahead, but pick the table decorations on the day by mood.
ESFJ>ISFP.worry: You fill your schedule with plans for others and sometimes can't make time for yourself. You can't say no when asked, so your weekends fill up fast.
ESFJ>ISFP.karai: Plans with others get set right away, but plans just for you rarely make it onto the calendar.
ESFJ>ISFP.aru: After having friends over and looking after everyone, you make your favorite tea and relax on your own.
ESFJ>ISFP.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energy from being with people, makes plans, and does things properly. As the years went by, you also came to recharge with time alone doing what you love and going with your mood. Your love of looking after people hasn't changed. While you're looking after others, your head is full of them, so when it's over, you want to take some time alone with your favorite tea to recharge.
ESFJ>ISFP.yure: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your hosting-friends self or your relaxing-alone self.
ESFJ>ISFP.plus: You can't make time for yourself because you love doing things for others. When people get together at your place, everyone can relax.
ESFJ>ISFP.tip: Put just one plan for yourself in your calendar first. It'll give you real rest, better than "if I feel like it."
ESFJ>ISFP.hidden: Do you naturally get energy when everyone gathers? That's your temperament, which gets energy from people. Use it, and you can share the things you enjoy alone with others too.

ESFJ>ESTP.title: Someone who asks "Are you okay?" and then moves fast.
ESFJ>ESTP.body: When something happens, you look out for the people around you and can move right away. If it looks like rain, you might buy umbrellas at the convenience store for the people around you too. Even if you forget gear on a camping trip, you quickly look up a nearby store and work it out.
ESFJ>ESTP.say: "The trains are stopped? Then let's take a taxi."
ESFJ>ESTP.say_s: "The trains are stopped? Then let's take the bus."
ESFJ>ESTP.do: When you learn it'll rain on the day of an event, you switch to the rainy-day plan right away.
ESFJ>ESTP.worry: Sometimes you move so fast that you push ahead before asking how the other person feels. You want to keep to your plans, but sometimes you want to change them on the spot.
ESFJ>ESTP.karai: While worrying about everyone, in your head you're already thinking about what to do next.
ESFJ>ESTP.aru: When a friend calls you feeling down, before even hearing them out, you're already moving: "Want me to come over now?"
ESFJ>ESTP.why: By birth, you're the type who values the other person's feelings and prepares ahead of time. As you gained experience, you also came to think about what would help most in the moment and act on it right away. Your caring nature has been there all along; what's grown is how fast you get moving. When you can tell from someone's voice on the phone that they're having a hard time, you feel that going to see them will help more than listening, and your body moves first.
ESFJ>ESTP.yure: Two parts are different: deciding with logic or with feelings, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Answer as your handling-trouble self and you lean toward logic and the moment. Answer as your listening-to-a-friend self and you lean toward feelings and planning.
ESFJ>ESTP.plus: You move fast because you want to help people in trouble quickly. It's reassuring to have someone who acts first when something happens.
ESFJ>ESTP.tip: When someone's in trouble, after "Are you okay?" add, "What would you like to do?" before acting. You can help in a way that fits how they feel.
ESFJ>ESTP.hidden: Do you get your plans and things ready by the day before? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Because of it, you can act calmly even when something sudden comes up.

ESFJ>ESFP.title: Someone who books early, then enjoys detours on the day.
ESFJ>ESFP.body: You get everything ready early, then enjoy the moment to the fullest on the day. You take care of the restaurant reservation and messaging everyone the week before, so on the day you hardly look at the clock. When someone's laughing, you get louder too. When you find a place that looks good on a trip, you might say, "Let's try it," even if it wasn't in the plan.
ESFJ>ESFP.say: "How's this outfit? I wore it because I wanted to show everyone!"
ESFJ>ESFP.do: At your kid's sports day, you prepare the lunch properly and you're the loudest one cheering.
ESFJ>ESFP.do_s: On field day, you get your class's headbands ready properly and you're the loudest one cheering.
ESFJ>ESFP.worry: Sometimes you're having so much fun that you stay longer than planned. Some days you go back and forth between sticking to the plan and enjoying the moment.
ESFJ>ESFP.karai: On the very day you say, "I'm leaving early today," you stay till the end.
ESFJ>ESFP.aru: You booked the restaurant for six, but before that you say, "Let's stop by the crepe stand for a bit."
ESFJ>ESFP.why: By birth, you're the type who makes plans and sticks to them. As you gained experience, you also became able to jump right in on fun things you find in the moment. Making sure the important reservations are in hasn't changed. Since the six o'clock reservation is set and you feel at ease, until then your attention drifts to whatever tasty thing is right in front of you.
ESFJ>ESFP.yure: Only one part is different: sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture preparing for an event and you answer like a planner. Picture heading out for fun and you answer like someone who goes with the flow.
ESFJ>ESFP.plus: You stay longer because you love spending time with everyone. With someone who prepares properly and has the most fun on the day, the room lights up.
ESFJ>ESFP.tip: On days out, decide just one thing: "I'll head home at this time." Until then, you can fully enjoy your detours.
ESFJ>ESFP.hidden: Do you take care of reservations and what to bring ahead of time? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Because of it, everyone can take detours with peace of mind on the day.
